scores.claim_text: Direct Funding Agreement with U.S. Department of Commerce that restricts share buybacks/dividends (likely CHIPS Act solar-cell industrial-base award supporting Albuquerque SolAero facility).
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_recipient_grants + contracts (Rocket Lab, SolAero, Department of Commerce)
scores.interpretation: UNVERIFIED. The Direct Funding Agreement with Commerce is disclosed only in passing (as a dividend/buyback restriction) but no specific dollar amount, program name, or award date is given. USAspending shows zero Commerce awards to Rocket Lab USA or to SolAero Technologies. CHIPS Act / industrial-base awards often take 6-12 months to post in USAspending after announcement, and the agreement's existence is corroborated only by the negative-covenant text in the 10-K itself. Not a hard contradiction (Heuristic 7 not triggered because no dollar amount was asserted), but the lack of any independent footprint is a moderate amber flag worth tracking; if no related Commerce-CHIPS line item appears post-cutoff, this would migrate to MODERATE.

scores.claim_text: Neutron medium-lift vehicle (13,000 kg reusable to LEO) under development at LC-3 Wallops; Jan 21 2026 Stage 1 tank ruptured in hydro qual test, impacting launch schedule; securities class action re Neutron progress representations.

M_value.securities_class_action_status: Motion to Dismiss granted Nov 10 2025; amended complaint filed Dec 19 2025; second MTD filed Jan 19 2026
M_value.lc3_status: expected in service in 2026; under construction

scores.interpretation: MODERATE per Calibration Heuristic 3 (planned-vs-operational with EXTRA WEIGHT). Neutron is squarely in the 'design/prototype' stage of the stage ladder — not yet first-launched. The Jan 2026 tank rupture is candidly disclosed as a subsequent event, and the 8-K trail confirms timely public disclosure. However, the existence of a securities class action specifically alleging misstatements about Neutron development progress is a real signal that prior public communications may have overstated readiness; the case had survived to amended-complaint stage as of cutoff. Score MODERATE because: (a) the 10-K itself is honest about the slip; (b) the still-pending litigation indicates the market is testing the prior optimism; (c) Neutron 2026 service entry now looks optimistic given Q1 tank failure. Not SEVERE because disclosure is contemporaneous and concrete.

scores.interpretation: PASS. The CAPSTONE lunar pathfinder claim — the only specific Artemis-related claim in the 10-K — is independently confirmed in USAspending (NASA award 80KSC020C0002 for $10.07M, CISLUNAR AUTONOMOUS POSITIONING SYSTEM TECHNOLOGY OPERATIONS AND NAVIGATION EXPERIMENT LAUNCH SERVICE). Defense-prime corroboration is null (LMT/NOC/RTX 10-Ks do not mention 'Rocket Lab'), but the 10-K does not name any specific prime as a material customer — it only generically references 'aerospace prime contractors' — so Heuristic 7 absence-while-naming is not triggered.

M_value.Long_Beach_CA: not in FRS under Rocket Lab name

scores.interpretation: PASS with caveat. The two purely commercial industrial sites that RKLB operates as principal — the SolAero solar-cell fab in Albuquerque and the composite production complex in Middle River MD — both appear in EPA FRS under exactly the names and addresses claimed. The non-appearance of Long Beach (likely office/light-mfg), Stennis (NASA leasehold, registers under NASA), Wallops (NASA leasehold), and the Tucson GEOST site (recent acquisition Aug 2025) is consistent with their facility-ownership status rather than a fabrication. Heuristic 1 (EPA-FRS scope) test passes: at least two claimed industrial facilities are independently verified.
